reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through the November 5 close: SPX 7,353.73, down 6.26% from its 120-day high, 4.33% below its 50-day and 0.42% above its 200-day; SMH 447.73, down 33.36% from its high and below Zone 2 ($470-505), while NVDA 181.60 sits inside Zone 2 ($175-185); VIX closed 28.18, up 69.66% on the day, with high-yield OAS 3.48 calm and the mechanical capitulation tally at 2 of 4. The midday tape is bouncing (QQQ +1.79%, VIX 24.42 intraday) but the episode data is not stale — it is through Nov 5 and the bounce is unconfirmed.
reaction.invalidation: A daily close above the SPX 7,750-7,820 failure zone with SMH reclaiming $505 and VIX under 20 would prove the correction read wrong and void this ladder; conversely a sustained credit break (high-yield OAS above 4.0) voids the Watch stance toward full stand-down.

ladder.response: No new probes; hold cash in bills and wait for a second-low structure — the correction is deepening, not offering a buying opportunity.
ladder.trigger: SPX closes below its 200-day at 7,322.74, or SMH closes below $440

ladder.response: Treat as a sell-the-rally zone, not a re-entry; no adds into the failure zone until a close above it with VIX under 20.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone, or SMH rallies toward 580-600 and stalls

ladder.response: Full stand-down: no probes of any kind; the correction has become a credit event and this ladder is void.

ladder.response: Re-arm the Tranche A probe on the ladder's terms — starter size only, limit at the zone top.

reaction.trapRisk: The midday bounce (QQQ +1.79%, VIX down 13.34% intraday to 24.42) is the first bounce after the November 5 washout, and the washout itself showed no climax reversal — SMH volume ran 2.86x its 20-day average but closed in the bottom 6% of its range, VIX at its 5-day high. The pivot-and-fail pattern is the base case for this bounce: a stall into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone that rolls over. No chasing the first bounce and no probe on the NVDA Zone 2 print alone — entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict and a second low that holds.

strategyPosture: Watch. Tranche A stays void — SMH closed below its $470 Zone 2 floor, the mechanical tally is 2 of 4, and VIX closed 28.18, above the 25 stand-down line. The midday bounce is the first bounce, not a confirmation: no chasing, no probe until a fresh Zone 2 print plus a tally of 3 or better and VIX back under 25.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking: if credit flips — high-yield OAS above 4.0 or lending standards tightening toward the ~40% stress threshold — rotation becomes rollover fast. For now the data backs the rotation read, but the Mag7 drawdown is deep enough that a second leg down in the leaders would drag the index with it.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average 16.93% below their 52-week highs against SPY 5.6% below its high — an 11.33-point divergence gap — while bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold, and high-yield OAS is 3.48 and calm. The weakest leader is GOOGL at -30% from its high; the strongest is AAPL at -3.2%.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The index looks calm — SPY only 5.6% off its high and +0.67% at midday — while the market's leadership bleeds: the Mag7 complex is on average nearly 17% below its highs.
themes.watchFor: High-yield OAS breaking above 4.0 or lending standards tightening would flip rotation into rollover.

themes.counterRead: Zone breaks are the discipline, not the buying signal: SMH below its $470 floor voids Tranche A, and the NVDA Zone 2 print alone does not re-arm anything — the morning probe was retracted for exactly this reason. The opportunity is real but the entry is gated: a fresh Zone 2 close plus tally 3 of 4 plus VIX under 25.
themes.dataAnchor: SMH is 33.36% below its 120-day high and below Zone 2 at $447.73; NVDA sits in Zone 2 at $181.60 (-25.38% from high, live $187.53, RSI 31.6); MU is $690.93, -44.9% from its high with RSI 31.4 and -33.3% over one month. Against that, revenue is still growing: NVDA +61.4% YoY, AVGO +55%, LRCX +131.3%, CLS +66.8%. Top conviction scores: AVGO 85, DDOG 84, ONTO 83, VRT 81.
themes.label: AI infrastructure washout
themes.narrative: The AI complex has been cut by a third from its highs and the tape reads like the trade is over — semis are the weakest leg, SMH down 11.21% on November 5 alone.
themes.watchFor: SMH closing back inside Zone 2 ($470-505) with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better.

themes.counterRead: The Texas election vote is a genuine policy overhang on data-center power demand, not just sentiment — it is the reason VST fell 14% into the report. The bounce says the market is treating the report as the settler; if the policy risk hardens into an actual moratorium push, the snapback reverses. Size nothing on the bounce alone.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is +9.75% at midday, OKLO +23.55%, SMR +16.02% — but one-month damage is deep: VST -20.65%, OKLO -31.38%, SMR -30.74%. VST's fundamentals at the trough: revenue +19.1% YoY, P/S 2.4x, insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, conviction score 80.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power snapback
themes.narrative: The power leg of the AI trade is snapping back hard at midday after the Texas election vote knocked VST down 14% into its November 6 report — the report is what the drop had to settle.
themes.watchFor: Whether the VST bounce holds through the close and whether the Texas data-center policy risk advances beyond election rhetoric.

themes.counterRead: Multiple compression can persist even with revenue recovering — the board itself is not promoting: conviction promotions are empty and the top names sit on the watchlist, not the board. The setup is a research queue, not a buy list, until a name clears the promotion gate with a verified entry.
themes.dataAnchor: DDOG is -39.6% from its high with RSI 29.5 while revenue grows 27.7% YoY at 80% gross margin (conviction score 84); SNOW is -27.9% from its high with revenue +34.3% (score 76); NOW is -41.7% from its high with RSI 27.7; MDB is -34.2% with revenue +28% (score 68). themes.label: Software / SaaS at the trough
themes.narrative: Enterprise software is priced like a broken trade — DDOG, SNOW and NOW are 28-42% below their highs on oversold RSIs — while the revenue lines keep growing 28-34% a year.
themes.watchFor: A conviction promotion off the watchlist — DDOG or SNOW clearing the board's entry gate with a verified level.

themes.counterRead: The bounce has real breadth behind it — OKLO +23.55%, SMR +16.02%, RKLB +13.5%, VST +9.75% at midday is buying, not just short-covering. But breadth on day one of a bounce is what traps look like: the washout printed no climax reversal and no VIX rollover, so this bounce has to prove itself with a second low that holds.
themes.dataAnchor: SPY +0.67% and QQQ +1.79% at midday, VIX down 13.34% intraday to 24.42 — after a November 5 close of 28.18 (+69.66%), the 5-day high, with SPX -4.36% on the day. The washout showed no reversal: SMH volume 2.86x its 20-day average but the close in the bottom 6% of its range, and the mechanical tally stuck at 2 of 4 (zone occupancy and credit calm confirmed; volume-climax reversal and VIX rollover not).
themes.label: First bounce, not a bottom
themes.narrative: The midday tape reads like relief — indexes green, VIX collapsing off its high — and the temptation is to call November 5 the bottom.
themes.watchFor: Whether the bounce holds into the close or stalls into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone, and whether a second low forms and holds.
